blocks.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions. Write True or False for the true-false questions.

stimulus.text:
A big mango tree stands beside the hill road near Kesari village. Nobody knows who planted it. It is older than Grandfather. Every summer, its branches bend low with yellow mangoes.

The whole village shares the tree. Each family picks mangoes on one day of the week only. On Monday, it is Meena’s family. On Tuesday, it is the potter’s family. The headman rings a brass bell at sunrise to mark the day. Children may collect fallen mangoes at any time. They must not shake the branches.

Travellers rest in the cool shade and eat one mango for free. In autumn, everyone digs the soil around the roots and adds fresh compost. “A tree that feeds us needs food too,” says the headman.

items.q: Where does the mango tree stand?
When does the headman ring the brass bell?
What must the children not do?
What can travellers do at the mango tree?
items.answer: They can rest in the cool shade (1) and eat one mango for free (1).

items.q: Write one thing the villagers do to keep the mango picking fair, and one thing they do to look after the tree.
items.answer: Fair picking (1): each family picks on its own day of the week, or the headman rings a bell to mark the day, or children do not shake the branches (any one). Looking after the tree (1): in autumn they dig the soil around the roots, or they add fresh compost (any one).

answerPoints.point: One way of keeping the picking fair
One way of looking after the tree

items.skill: reading: two facts from two places

items.q: The villagers know who planted the mango tree.
items.answer: False. Nobody knows who planted it.

items.q: Children may collect fallen mangoes at any time.
On which day of the week does Meena’s family pick mangoes?
Which family picks mangoes on Tuesday?
What colour are the mangoes on the tree?
What do the villagers add to the soil around the roots in autumn?

blocks.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions. Write True or False for the true-false questions. For the fill-in-the-blank questions, use a word from the text.

stimulus.text: Our village pond is home to many fish. The elders fish there only twice a month. They lift the nets gently and throw the small fish back. Children feed the fish quietly, so the fish do not swim away. Last summer, a few boys fished greedily and took too many. The pond looked almost empty. The elders spoke kindly to the boys. Now everyone waits for the fishing day, and the fish swim happily again.

items.q: Write two ways in which the elders take care of the fish in the pond.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): they fish only twice a month; they lift the nets gently; they throw the small fish back.

items.q: What happened when a few boys fished greedily?
items.answer: The boys took too many fish (1) and the pond looked almost empty (1).

items.q: How did the elders speak to the boys, and what does everyone do now?
items.answer: The elders spoke kindly to the boys (1). Now everyone waits for the fishing day (1).

answerPoints.point: They spoke kindly to the boys
Everyone waits for the fishing day

items.skill: reading: two facts from two places

items.q: The elders lift the nets _____.
The children feed the fish _____.
After the boys took too many fish, the pond looked almost _____.
The elders fish in the pond every day.
items.answer: False. They fish only twice a month.

items.q: The elders were angry and shouted at the boys.
items.answer: False. They spoke kindly to the boys.

items.q: Which word from the text tells how the boys fished?

blocks.instruction: Answer in one word or a few words.

items.q: Who said, “I have never eaten such juicy green leaves”?
Which animal asked the stag how he was?
What did some of the animals bring for the sick stag?
Why did the old stag stop going down the hillock to meet his friends?
items.answer: He had fallen ill (1) and he was too weak to come down (1).

answerPoints.point: He was too weak to come down

items.q: Why did the sick stag eat the tender grass and rest for a while?
items.answer: He knew that fresh, healthy food (1) and proper rest (1) would help him get better.

answerPoints.point: Fresh, healthy food would help him get well
Proper rest would help him get well

items.q:
Put these events in the order in which they happened in the story. Write the four letters in order.
(a) The grass grew back after the rain.
(b) The stag fell ill.
(c) The animals ate the fresh grass on the hillock.
(d) The animals decided to find food elsewhere.
items.answer: b, c, d, a. (b) The stag fell ill; (c) the animals ate the grass on the hillock; (d) they decided to find food elsewhere; (a) the grass grew back after the rain. Split: b then c in the right order — 1; d then a in the right order — 1.

answerPoints.point: (b) before (c) placed correctly at the start
(d) before (a) placed correctly at the end

items.markingGuide: Correct order b, c, d, a — 2; the first two or the last two events in the right order — 1; neither — 0. Maximum 2.

items.q: How did the animals feel when they understood what they had done to the stag? What had made them forget their friend?
items.answer: They felt ashamed (1). Their greed had made them forget their friend (1).

answerPoints.point: Their greed made them forget the stag

items.q: What would you do if you were visiting an ill friend and saw only one plate of fruit beside the bed? Write two sentences.
items.answer: Model answer: I would leave the fruit for my friend. I would sit quietly and ask how my friend feels.

answerPoints.point: A sensible, kind action in a full sentence
A second sensible action or reason in a full sentence

items.markingGuide: Two sensible, kind answers in full sentences — 2; one answer, or two answers that are not in full sentences — 1; unrelated or selfish answer with no reason — 0. Accept any answer that thinks of the ill friend. Maximum 2.

blocks.instruction: Write five sentences on ONE of the two topics.

items.q:
Write five sentences about a shady tree or a garden near your home.
OR
Write five sentences about how you help a friend who is ill.
items.answer: Model answer (garden): There is a small garden near my house. It has a big neem tree. The shady spot under the tree is cool. Birds sing there in the morning. I play there with my friends every evening.

answerPoints.point: Sentence 1 — complete and on the topic
Sentence 2 — complete and on the topic
Sentence 3 — complete and on the topic
Sentence 4 — complete and on the topic
Sentence 5 — complete and on the topic

items.markingGuide: One mark for each complete sentence on the chosen topic, up to 5. Deduct 1 for more than three mistakes in spelling, capital letters or full stops. Fewer than five sentences: give one mark per good sentence. Maximum 5.

blocks.instruction: Complete the paragraph by following the hints.

items.q:
Write a short paragraph about a helper you see every day, such as a postman, a gardener or a milkman. Follow these four hints, one sentence for each.
1. Say who the helper is and what work the helper does.
2. Say when the helper comes and how the helper works. Use an adverb of manner, such as carefully or cheerfully.
3. Say how the people in your lane greet the helper.
4. Say why you like the helper.
items.answer: Model answer: Our postman is Ramesh uncle. He brings letters and parcels to every house. He comes at ten o’clock and puts the letters carefully into the letter box. People in our lane greet him warmly. I like him because he is always cheerful and helpful.

answerPoints.point: Hint 1 — the helper and the work, in a full sentence
Hint 2 — the time and an adverb of manner used correctly
Hint 3 — how people greet the helper
Hint 4 — a reason for liking the helper

items.markingGuide: One mark for each hint answered in a full sentence, up to 4. The adverb of manner in hint 2 must be spelt and used correctly, or that mark is lost. Deduct 1 for more than three mistakes in spelling or punctuation. Maximum 4.

blocks.instruction: Make a sentence with each word.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word: stag
items.answer: Model answer: The stag stood on the hill and looked at the valley.
items.markingGuide: A complete, sensible sentence that uses the word stag correctly — 1; the word is missing, misused, or the sentence is not complete — 0. Maximum 1.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word: tender
items.answer: Model answer: The goat ate the tender leaves of the young plant.
items.markingGuide: A complete, sensible sentence that uses the word tender correctly (soft and young) — 1; the word is missing, misused, or the sentence is not complete — 0. Maximum 1.

items.q: Make a sentence with the word: cheerfully
items.answer: Model answer: The children sang cheerfully on the bus.
items.markingGuide: A complete, sensible sentence in which cheerfully tells how something is done — 1; the word is missing, misused, or the sentence is not complete — 0. Maximum 1.

blocks.instruction: Choose the correct word from the brackets and fill in the blanks.

items.q: The tortoise walked _____ across the road. (slow / slowly)
Kavya read the poem _____ so that everyone could hear. (loud / loudly)
Grandmother sings _____ in the kitchen. (soft / softly)
The gardener watered the _____ plants. (healthy / healthily)
The _____ shopkeeper gave the child a free sweet. (friendly / friend)

Change the word in brackets into an adverb and rewrite the sentence.
The girl sang (sweet).
items.answer: The girl sang sweetly. (Also accept: The girl sweetly sang.) Split: adverb sweetly spelt correctly — 1; the rest of the sentence written correctly with a capital letter and full stop — 1.

answerPoints.point: Full sentence copied correctly with capital letter and full stop

items.q:
Change the word in brackets into an adverb and rewrite the sentence.
Meera closed the gate (careful).
items.answer: Meera closed the gate carefully. (Also accept: Meera carefully closed the gate.) Split: adverb carefully spelt correctly — 1; the rest of the sentence written correctly with a capital letter and full stop — 1.

answerPoints.point: Full sentence copied correctly with capital letter and full stop

items.q: Write two sentences about a rabbit. In the first sentence use the word quick to describe the rabbit. In the second sentence use the word quickly to tell how the rabbit ran.
items.answer: Model answer: The rabbit is quick. The rabbit ran quickly into the bush. Split: quick describes the rabbit, e.g. a quick rabbit or the rabbit is quick — 1; quickly tells how the rabbit ran — 1.

answerPoints.point: A sentence in which quick describes the rabbit
A sentence in which quickly tells how the rabbit ran

items.markingGuide: First sentence uses quick as a describing word — 1; second sentence uses quickly to tell how the rabbit ran — 1. Each sentence must be complete. Maximum 2.
items.chapterSource: Let us Learn B and C

items.q:
Write the adverb of manner in the sentence, and the action word it tells more about.
The nurse spoke kindly to the sick child.

Two of these words tell how something is done. Write the two words.
soon   quickly   nearby   cheerfully   early
items.answer: quickly (1) and cheerfully (1), in any order.

items.q:
Write the describing word in each sentence.
(a) The friendly animals came to visit.
(b) We rested in a shaded spot.

Each sentence has a mistake in the word that tells how. Rewrite each sentence correctly.
(a) The bus moved slow up the hill.
(b) The teacher spoke kind to the little girl.
items.answer: (a) The bus moved slowly up the hill. (1) (b) The teacher spoke kindly to the little girl. (1)

answerPoints.point: (a) slow changed to slowly; rest of sentence correct
(b) kind changed to kindly; rest of sentence correct

blocks.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

items.q: Match each describing phrase with its meaning.
items.answer: lush garden — thick, green and full of plants; tender leaves — soft and young; shaded lane — a path that has shade from trees; friendly neighbour — kind and pleasant to people; healthy breakfast — food that keeps the body strong.

pairs.right: thick, green and full of plants
a path that has shade from trees
food that keeps the body strong

items.chapterSource: Let us Learn A and B

blocks.instruction: Fill in the blanks using the words from the box.

items.q:
Word box: hillock   sheltering   recovery
The old shed is _____ the goats from the rain. A small _____ rises behind the shed.

Word box: stag   recovery   lush
Dadi made a quick _____ after her fever. Now she walks in the _____ green garden.

Write the opposite word for each.
(a) quickly   (b) loudly
items.markingGuide: (a) slowly — 1; (b) quietly or softly — 1. Accept any clear opposite of the meaning. Maximum 2.

items.q: Write one sentence with the phrase shaded spot and one sentence with the phrase lush forest. Each sentence must show what the phrase means.
items.answer: Model answer: We sat in a shaded spot under the neem tree to keep cool. The lush forest was thick with green trees and plants. Split: each sentence — 1.

answerPoints.point: A sentence that shows the meaning of shaded spot
A sentence that shows the meaning of lush forest

items.markingGuide: A complete sentence that shows the meaning of shaded spot (a place with shade) — 1; a complete sentence that shows the meaning of lush forest (thick and green) — 1. Maximum 2.

items.q: Circle the correct spelling.
Circle the correct spelling.
Circle the correct spelling.

blocks.instruction: Rearrange the jumbled letters to make a meaningful word.

items.q: Jumbled word: ulyodl. Write the word (starts with l; an adverb).

answerPoints.point: Letters in the right order, spelt correctly

items.q: Jumbled word: yhalthe. Write the word (starts with h; a describing word).

answerPoints.point: Letters in the right order, spelt correctly

items.q: Jumbled word: lyfdrine. Write the word (starts with f; a describing word).

answerPoints.point: Letters in the right order, spelt correctly

blocks.instruction: Write the following lines in neat handwriting.

stimulus.text: After the rain, the garden looked fresh and green. Two sparrows sat on a shaded branch and sang cheerfully. The gardener smiled and watered the plants gently.

items.q: Write the passage in neat handwriting.
items.answer: A neat, evenly spaced copy of the passage with correct capital letters and full stops.
items.markingGuide: Letters well formed, evenly spaced and on the line, with capital letters and full stops in the right places — 3; mostly neat with two or three slips — 2; hard to read or copied with many slips — 1. Deduct 1 if the copy is not finished. Maximum 3.

blocks.instruction: Write the following lines in neat handwriting.

stimulus.text: Our postman rides a red cycle. He rings the bell twice and calls out our names. We take the letters carefully and thank him with a smile.

items.q: Write the passage in neat handwriting.
items.answer: A neat, evenly spaced copy of the passage with correct capital letters and full stops.
items.markingGuide: Letters well formed, evenly spaced and on the line, with capital letters and full stops in the right places — 3; mostly neat with two or three slips — 2; hard to read or copied with many slips — 1. Deduct 1 if the copy is not finished. Maximum 3.
